title: Hydration Mismatches & Client-Only Value Evaluation
content: React components rendered on the server must produce an identical initial HTML structure to what is mounted on the client. Evaluating non-deterministic values like window, document, localStorage, or new Date().toLocaleTimeString() directly in JSX triggers React Error #418 (Hydration Failed). Solution: Wrap browser-only reads in useEffect or use dynamic import with ssr: false.

title: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) & Preflight Options
content: CORS is a browser security protocol that prevents malicious scripts on one origin from making unauthorized API requests to a different origin. When requests include custom headers (e.g. Authorization Bearer) or methods other than GET/POST/HEAD, the browser issues a preflight HTTP OPTIONS request. The server must return 200/204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Methods, and Access-Control-Allow-Headers.

title: CSS Stacking Context Rules & Z-Index Invalidation
content: A local Stacking Context is formed by any element with opacity < 1, transform != none, filter != none, or position: fixed. Once formed, all child elements are contained inside that local layer; child z-indexes cannot escape to compete with sibling elements outside the stacking context. Solution: Use React Portals (createPortal) to render modals directly under document.body.

title: Too Many Re-renders: Synchronous setState in Render Body
content: Calling a state setter (like setCount) synchronously inside the body of a component function triggers an immediate re-render before React can finish the current render cycle, causing an infinite loop. Solution: Either calculate derived state as a simple variable, or move the setState call inside a useEffect hook or event handler.

title: Optional Chaining & Nullish Coalescing for Async Collections
content: In asynchronous UI rendering, collections retrieved via API (like products or users) are initially undefined before the network promise resolves. Calling .map() on undefined causes an uncaught TypeError crash. Solution: Initialize state with an empty array (useState([])), or use optional chaining (products?.map(...)) with a loading skeleton fallback.

title: Asynchronous Memory Leaks & Cleanup Functions
content: When a component unmounts while an asynchronous operation is in flight, setting state on the unmounted component wastes resources and triggers React warnings. Solution: Use an AbortController in fetch or a boolean flag (let isMounted = true) that is toggled to false inside the useEffect return cleanup function.
